articleTitle: A Large-Loop Antenna for Magnetic Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of a large loop antenna for magnetic field measurements is analyzed. The method offers considerable advantages over the usual method of measurement at a distance. The sensitivity is high and external influences are of minor importance, even in an environment where high ambient signals exist (e.g. radio signals). Computations show a nearly flat frequency response in the 9kHz to 30MHz range. An unambiguous correlation with other measurement methods is obtained.

articleTitle: Progress Report on a Different Kind of ESD Standard
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A working group of the IEEE Surge Protective Devices Committee was formed to prepare a standard in the form of a Guide, describing the various manifestations of electrostatic discharge (ESD). The ESDs with which the Guide is concerned are initiated by humans or mobile furnishings, and affect an electronic equipment victim.[1] The Guide's purpose is not to generate another equipment ESD test standard, but rather to help provide firmer theoretical and practical bases for developing and evaluating such standards. The work is now in progress, and this paper is a status report on the present draft document that has resulted. The draft Guide incorporates standardized terminology and some ESD event models. It has also characterized ESDs in three different voltage regimes, has made a start in relating multiple ESDs to slow and fast discharge current fronts, and includes some characterizations of ESD-generated electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: An Advanced Electromagnetic Interference Meter for the Twenty-First Century
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The concept of an advanced, near-real-time electromagnetic interference (EMI) meter is described. Its genesis is traced from current EMI meter technology through a "bank-of-filters” technique and a FFT/DFT analyzer to a conceptual model near-real-time EMI meter in which the Fourier transform is convoluted with desireable detector functions and indicator constraints. Such convolutions will provide for rapidly measuring the peak, quasi—peak, rms, or average of the input electromagnetic signals and noise, and also simulate special level indicator characteristics, e.g., a D'Arsonval instrument.

articleTitle: Worldwide Enhancement of National Spectrum Management Systems
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to enhance national spectrum management systems throughout the world administrations should improve management procedures and automate standard data files and EMC analysis techniques. Spectrum management activities and techniques, clerical, licensing, frequency assignment and monitoring operations, data file and computer software and hardware requirements are described. Criteria for computer automation are given. It is concluded that the cost of computer hardware is the lowest overall cost in automating a national spectrum management system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Various Absorber Materials in the Frequency Range 30-300 MHz
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to investigate the behaviour of absorber lined chambers, a simple measuring method, with a transmissionline cell, is used to evaluate the performance of various absorber configurations and materials in the frequency range 30-300 MHz. The measurement results clearly show the origin of the often poor low-frequency behaviour of anechoic chambers. Some absorber configurations are found to be a more favorite remedy to this low-frequency problem than others. Furthermore, a lumped element network representation of the absorber is described with which the behaviour of the absorber configurations can be predicted and optimised.

articleTitle: The Electromagnetic Enviroment in the Area of Railway Stations at 16,66 Hz
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic disturbances caused by low-frequency magnetic fields occurs when constructing buildings over railway tracks with electric traction (Fig. 1). All these buildings are set up with electronic equipment, especially with computer terminals. The magnetic field deflects the electron beam of the CRT and the perceptability of the characters on the screen becomes worse. The goal of the investigation was a realistic estimation of the intensity of the magnetic field. The field is created by an extended loop consisting of the contact wire and the rail return. The calculation cannot be done very exactly because there is little knowledge about the current distribution between the rails and the earth. In the area on the platform extensive measurements of the variation of amplitude in time and the corresponding current in the contact wire were carried out. Realistic values of the induction are very important because all shielding measures depend on these values.

articleTitle: Reflections on Screening
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses theories of screening (shielding) by reflection and the application of the wave impedance concept. Reference is made to correlation between measurements of screening effectiveness under near and far field conditions and experimental results are quoted to show good agreement between the two for screening in the magnetic mode.

articleTitle: Antenna-to-Antenna Interaction in the Presence of a Longitudinal Screen between Them
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The report gives some results of the theoretical and experimental investigation dedicated to the influence of longitudinal plates on electromagnetic interaction between antennas. There has been studied the attenuation of an electromagnetic field depending on geometric parameters of a plate, its location relative to antennas and wave length. It was shown that the given results prove the existence of field attenuation effect by means of longitudinal flat structures and the possibility of using this effect to suppress interference fields from the definite directions and electromagnetic decoupling of antennas.

articleTitle: On the use of Loop Antennas as Electromagnetic Pulse Probes
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this study consideration is focused on the properties of a circular loop antenna influenced by the electromagnetic pulse field. The current flowing through the antenna depends on the both electric and magnetic components of the electromagnetic pulse. At appropriate loading, loop antennas may act as probes for measuring the components of the electromagnetic pulse and for determining the electromagnetic field distribution in EMP simulators.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Excitation of a Wire Crossing a Long Slot in an Infinite Plane
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic excitation of a long wire crossing a long slot in a perfectly conducting plane is studied. Babinet's principle is used to determine the penetrant fields from the slot. The expressions of the current induced on the wire and the equivalent circuits for the slot excitation are presented. Approximate equivalent sources are obtained for finite length slot.

articleTitle: Correlation of Lightning Current and Electric Field Derivative
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Current (I) and current-derivative (dl/dt) measurements with submicrosecond time resolution were made on triggered lightning return-strokes at the Kennedy Space Centre (Florida) during the Sumner of 1985 and 1987 and at Saint-Privat d'Allier (France) during the Summer of 1986. The current was measured using a coaxial shunt and the current derivative with a wideband inductive sensor. Both sensors were located at the base of the lightning channel and were connected through fast analog fibre optic links to several fast transient digitisers and magnetic tape recorder. It was thus possible to record triggered lightning current variations over a large frequency range (I : DC to 30 MHz; dl/dt to 90 MHz). The peak-currents of the return-strokes varied between a few kiloamps and 60 kiloamps and the peak current-derivatives between a few tens of kiloamps/microsecond and 400 kilo· amps/microsecond. Current measurements are of the same order as those obtained before; the mean-value of the peak-currents is about 15 kiloamps, corresponding to the mean-value of the peak-current-derivatives about equal to 114 kiloamps/microsecond. These direct current-derivative measurements are the first ones obtained so far. They are much higher than they were expected to be; this is the main result of the present work allowing better characterisation of lightning current transitions. Electric field-derivatives were also measured simultaneously at close range from the discharge in 1985 and in 1986. Electric field-derivatives (dE/dt) and current-derivative (dl/dt) are roughly proportional. Assuming the "Transmission-line model”, the lightning current velocity, obtained from the ratio of dI/dt and dE/dt measurements, has a mean value equal to 2.8 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> m/s (s.d. = 0.4 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> m/s), which is about twice the velocity obtained by optical measurements. One of the likely reasons is that the current propagation could be faster in the first tens of meters above the ground.

articleTitle: General Methods for Protection of Electronics against Interference, Tested in High-Voltage Substations
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: J. N. A. M. Van Rooy
P. C. T. Van der Laan

abstract: We describe concepts that lead to the design of extended grounding structures for the protection of electronic equipment in large as well as small systems. The layout is based on the principle of closed current loops. Among design details presented is the calculation of the transfer impedance of conduits of various shapes. Actual implementation and measurements in HV-substations confirm the correctness of the concepts.

articleTitle: Measuring the Complex Surface Transfer Impedance: A Critical Review of Existing Methods
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For analysing the coupling to extended cable systems or investigating the coupling by transient signals to cables, it is necessary to know the surface transfer impedance Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> as an intrinsic property of the cable. Furthermore, it is important to have the full complex Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>. Several existing measurement test fixtures are examined as to whether they deliver Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> in complex form and as an intrinsic property of the cable. Error sources are discussed for the triaxial, terminated triaxial / quadraxial and MIL-Std. test fixtures. A modified version of the widely accepted standard IEC 96-1A procedure is shown which simplifies the measurement effort.

articleTitle: Voltage Surges Induced on Overhead Lines by a Nearby Lightning Stroke
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Calculation of voltage surges induced on overhead lines by a nearby lightning stroke is only possible by assuming appropriate models for the lightning discharge and induction effects. Voltage surges in overhead wires are calculated by the numerical solution of the transmission-line equations in time-domain with finit-difference method. The excitation of a line by an externally electromagnetic field results in source terms in one of the transmission-line equations. These terms are depending on the horizontal electric field in line direction along the line. The electric fields are calculated by using the Traveling Current Source Model (TCS-model) of HEIDLER assuming infinit earth conductivity.

articleTitle: Measured and Predicted Coupling of Electromagnetic Radiation INTO a Cylindrical Cavity through a Small Aperture
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A modal expansion technique is used to determine the modal coefficients of the electromagnetic field coupled into a closed circular cylindrical cavity. Of interest in this paper are the modes which are excited in the cylindrical cavity, and the relative strengths of those modes. The coefficients are found by combining various orthogonality properties of the fields with experimental measurements made of the intensity of the field in a single cross-section of the cavity using an infrared (IR) diagnostic technique. The field distributions are measured by detecting the absorbed heat in a lossy dielectric sheet placed in the particular cylindrical cross-section of interest. The lossy material is cut into strips and aligned to measure the magnitude of a given spatial electric field component. As a check on the modal extraction technique described above, theoretical methods are developed to predict the coefficients of the modes coupled into the cavity. The electric and magnetic fields are expanded in terms of solenoidal and irrotational eigenvectors to allow for an aperture to exist in the cylinder walls. The expansion is then matched to the fields in the aperture. The results of the two techniques are compared.

articleTitle: Solution of EMC Problems by System Dynamics Theory
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper system dynamics methods are used to solve the problems of EMC theory for the combination of jointly functioning stochastic systems. Each of them, being in the isolated state, functions with the required quality. Suggested methods of analysis and EMC provision are obtained as a result of comparison models examination. The latter (comparison models) are based on linear differential equations (LDE) describing the behaviour of two-moment cumulants of initial stochastic systems.

articleTitle: Transient Coupling to Loop Antennas
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we discuss methods for the time domain analysis of loop antenna structures and present experimental validation of key results. A Norton equivalent circuit is used for the antenna and the effects of point linear and nonlinear loading are described by multiple convolution integrals. Particular attention is paid to the effects of nonlinear resistive and capacitive loading and it is shown that long duration current flow can be induced by short pulse coupling. The theoretical predictions are compared with experimental measurements of loop current, measured on an indoor time domain range at R.S.R.E. Pershore.

articleTitle: Return-Stroke Initiation
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The far fields from a lightning return stroke are a function of the spatio-temporal distribution of the return-stroke currents. This paper introduces a conical-transmission-line model of the return stroke immediately following leader closure. Based on this model, return-stroke speed is computed as well as the far fields. The impact of this model, as well as other factors, on the far fields is estimated.

articleTitle: A 320-KW Power, Arbitrary Waveform Injection System
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Typical injection systems are either based on: high power generation of signals with form, frequency and overvoltage difficult to control; or, low power generation using digital synthesis and CW amplification (1 to 10 kW) of signals with adjustable parameters. The proposed system allows reaching very high power levels (320 kW) while maintaining control of the signal's shape (obtained through synthesis). It is based on pulsed distributed amplification of the signals, which yields high power from a compact system.

articleTitle: Non-Average Power Receptor Model Development for the Intrasystem EMC Analysis Program
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The development of a set of analytical models is discussed. The models can be easily integrated into the present US Air Force Intrasystem Electromagnetic Compatibility Analysis Program (IEMCAP) and permit an EMC assessment of devices whose susceptibility is related to energy, peak voltage/current, and risetime. These additional receptor sensitivity analysis modeling techniques are required by IEMCAP because of the expanded use of modern digital electronics in present and future military/commercial systems and the need to assess the effects of lightning, EMP, and intense microwave environments. The additional models will provide IEMCAP users a means of efficiently analyzing numerous electromagnetic interactions at the system and subsystem level to assure that EMC margins are achieved for average and non-average power conditions. The study was performed by Kaman Sciences Corporation for the USAF Ballistic Missile Organization and the Rome Air Development Center (Contract F-29601-85-C-0024).

articleTitle: Give up Radiation Testing in Favour of Conduction Testing
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is suggested to replace delicate, time-consuming radiation and field immunity testing by more simple and better reproducible conduction testing, which is often more representative. In view of the strong technical and management arguments in favour of this technique as well as of the existing knowledge, concerted efforts of the EMC community should be without further delay directed towards developing the corresponding standards. Cost- effective EMC design, immunity and lower emission, resulting in better protection of the radio spectrum are the advantages to be gained.

articleTitle: A Case Study of Power Line Filters
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design of a power line filter is a difficult task because impedances seen by it are not known. Moreover, insertion loss measured using some standard techniques may not be indicative of its performance in actual installation because of widely different operating conditions. This calls for special measurement methods which should provide results that correspond to actual performance. The purpose of this study is to optimise a filter circuit which can provide adequate attenuation for meeting CS01, CS02 and CS06 test requirements of MIL-STD-461/462 on dc power lines of aerospace electronic units. The paper first discusses various filter configurations and definition of attenuation as against often used insertion loss. This is followed by a description of methods of attenuation measurements and discussion of results. The paper concludes by bringing out merits of the optimum filter-configuration.

articleTitle: Generalized Coupling Theory: A Computer-Adapted Method for Solving Interference Problems
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper gives an outline of the basic ideas to be followed in solving interference problems. After an explanation on how interference problems may be described, and what the actual goal of any calculation is, the advantages and the disadvantages of conventional models are described. The power of modern computers forces a revision in the sense that complete and accurate models are no longer an academic task but the adequate tool for solving -interference problems in everyday work. In the new CCITT Directives this philosophy is used.

articleTitle: Early Time Performance at Large Distances of Periodic Arrays of Flat-Plate Conical Wave Launchers
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper is an extension of past work on this subject [1] which considered the performance of infinite planar arrays of interconnected planar biconical sources. In order to obtain an improved performance in the context of the rate of rise in the distant field, we have considered an array of conical wave launchers here. Formulae for the early-time rise of such arrays are developed, tabulated and plotted, as a function of normalized geometrical parameters of an individual launcher and the array.

articleTitle: Dynamic Threshold Voltage of Protective Spark Gaps at Different Steepnesses of the Stressing Surge Front
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The dynamic threshold voltage of spark gaps shows a considerable dependance on the steepness of the stressing surge front. Using spark gaps as protective elements the knowledge of their voltage-time-characteristic is very meaningful for the assessment of the protection level. Hence the dynamic threshold voltages of different principal types of protective spark gaps were determined. The front steepness of the linearly rising test impulse voltage covered a wide range from 0.1 kV/µs to 10 kV/ns.

articleTitle: Simplified Numerical Evaluation of Mutual Inductance for the use in EMC Interactive Software Tool
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the results of research concerning the development of an interactive software tool for research and design in the field of electromagnetic influences on telecommunication lines are presented. The analysis deals with methods involving numerical and software algorithms for simple, quick and still sufficiently accurate evaluation of complex mutual inductance. Refering to fundamental methods based on Carson's series a two-dimensional bicubic splines interpolation is proposed. An algorithm concerning the calculation of mean and integral of mutual inductance, for the cases of oblique exposures and crossings, is derived out of named two-dimensional interpolation of the original function. An analysis and evaluation regarding time consumption and accuracy is performed.

articleTitle: The Electromagnetic Impact on Cars and Their Safety
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This report describes the current problems of automobile industry, which arise from the increased use of electronics in automotive vehicles. We not only consider the interference spectrum, which can be found in densely populated areas, but also its possible effects on safety related electronics. In conclusion, Daimler Benz’s concept on EMC problems will be discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetospheric VLF/ELF Radio Noise
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Our recent achievements concerning the VLF/ ELF emissions in the magnetosphere, are summarized in the present paper. The subjects we treat here are (1) hiss-triggered chorus in the outer magnetosphere, (2) substorm-associated VLF/ELF emissions at medium latitudes and (3) equatorial VLF radio noises, and their properties and the physical implications on wave-particle interactions have been described.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Electromagnetic Compatibility of Reactive Power Compensation Devices Working in Nonsinusoidal Voltage Conditions
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The maintenance of the good compatibility of reactive power devices correcting the power factor of the group of linear and nonlinear loads is mostly the problem of limiting the voltage distortion in the nodes of the supply network to the standard values. Large nonlinear loads such as rectifiers, converters or arc furnaces are characterized by low power factor which force their users to compensate the excessive amount of reactive power consumption using the appropriate devices. Most popular in this field are capacitor banks /with or without regulation/. Connection to a point of the network the large capacitance branch, made in the aim to increase the power transmission efficiency often causes the rise of the voltage harmonic distortion level in the network due possible parallel resonances between the capacitive component and the supply inductance. The proper choice of the compensation capacitance value taking into account not only desired power factor correction but also the voltage distortion levels [1] and the harmonic current excessive flows may give the considerable improvement of the compensating devices compatibility. Such a choice based on optimization calculations is the subject of the presented paper.

articleTitle: Exposure to the near Field of an RF Plastic Sealer
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A procedure for evaluating exposure to the near-field of an RF plastic sealer is proposed. The sealer examined was of a sewing-machine-type operating at a frequency of 40 MHz. The field distribution of this sealer was measured with near-field strength monitors. The distribution was found to be approximately the same as that produced by a combination of electric and magnetic dipoles, the moments of which could be determined by a single-point measurement of electric and magnetic fields and the configuration of RF feed. For this dipole source model the specific absorption rate (SAR) of a human model was calculated using the Method of Moments. It may be concluded that the SAR distribution in a human model can be evaluated using an equivalent source model, at least for a sewing-machine-type RF sealer. A similar procedure may be applied to the fields generated by other types of sealers.

articleTitle: Experimental Evidence for Porpoising Coupling and Optimization in Braided Cables
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The magnitude and phase of a set of cable samples, chosen to provide examples of both aperture and porpoising coupling, were measured in a quadraxial test fixture. These measurements showed that the phase of the transfer impedance at high frequencies for aperture coupling was opposite to that from porpoising coupling. In addition, the magnitude decreased when the contributions were about equal. These measurements demonstrate that porpoising coupling exists and is as important as aperture coupling. These measurements also show how braided cables can be optimized.

articleTitle: Radiation from a Printed Circuit Board: Theory and Application
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A practical method for computing electric and magnetic fields from a printed circuit board is presented. Electric field radiation using this method is correlated with experimental results. An example of the method applied to digital electronics is given.

articleTitle: Extrapolation of Transient Emp Data, using Prony's Method for Poleextraction in the Time Domain
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, Prony's method for pole-extraction directly from transient data has been used as a means of extrapolating a truncated time record, thereby reducing the leakage error and improving the resolution of the estimated spectrum. Prony's method was used to estimate the poles, from sets of model-data generated by different SEM-models. Some general conclusions and numerical aspects on this pole-finding technique are outlined. It is concluded that if the poles can be accurately extracted, then the extrapolation approach will considerably improve the estimated spectrum's accuracy.

articleTitle: On the Reconstruction of a Transient Waveform from Spectral Magnitude Data
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper investigates the possibility of reconstructing phase information from a measurement of the magnitude of a complex-valued spectrum of an EMP response of an electrical system. Once the phase is evaluated, the transient response may be computed using the Fourier transform. This technique involves the use of a Hilbert transform and an assumption of minimum phase, which ultimately provides a limitation to the accuracy of the phase reconstruction. In this paper, the calculational techniques are briefly outlined and several sample waveforms are processed in order to provide an illustration of the errors involved in this process.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Coupling into Wires
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Numerical simulations of the coupling of electromagnetic fields into wires are presented. The results were obtained using transmission-line modelling and three different modelling schemes, namely separated, integrated and diakoptic solution methods. The assumptions and accuracy implications of each method are discussed. Results are also included from wire scattering configurations, and are compared with available data.

articleTitle: Survey of Session: EMC in Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since the beginning of electric power transmission including generation and distribution, the main "noise source" in the sense of EMC were the lightning discharge phenomena producing very high overvoltages within the transmission systems. This short-duration overvoltages, quite often enhanced by traveling - wave phenomena and reflections within the transmission lines, can stress the insulation within all system elements to such a degree that the breakdown of the insulation and by this the interruption or the "blackout" of the electric power transmission was a quite common event. Today, the thunderstorms and the accompanying lightning strokes are still impinging on our transmission systems as in earlier times, but we have learned to protect the systems by adequate means so that the lightning event, though still being dangerous, is not any more the main source of failures within our power networks. An essential contribution to our knowledge in lightning protection of transmission systems can be alloted to the early investigations of Prof. Dr. Karl Berger, who just a few weeks before was able to celebrate his 90. birthday in Zollikon close to Zurich. About sixty years ago, he started to measure lightning and other overvoltages here in Switzerland by means of newly developed "cold cathode ray oscilloscopes", and yet today the results of these measurements are striking and very valuable to read (see e.g. /1/, /2/).

articleTitle: A Proposal for Estimating Pantograph Discharge Rate using Noise Currents
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a new method for estimating the arc discharge rate using the noise currents flowing through the pantograph. The estimation principle is based on the statistical discrimination of the arc durations from the digital measurement values of the BPF envelope responses to the noise currents in the VHF band at the single frequency. For verifying the validity of this method, the experiment is performed by using the sliding-contact apparatus which is well known as a model of the current collector of an electric car.

articleTitle: The Effects of Resonance in Cable-to-Cable Coupling
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This lecture focuses on the mathematical methods and the test procedures to determine the coupling attenuation between shielded cables installed in parallel. The proof by measuring performed to reveal that pregiven EMC limits for items of equipment to be installed and incorporated in a system could be kept does in itself not yet ensure the EMC of the overall system. The purpose of the activities performed and described herein was to investigate and provide suitable means of reducing EMC influences, with special emphasis on cables required for the comprehensive interconnection to the individual items of equipment. The results achieved showed that electromagnetic coupling causing unacceptable interferences can be reduced substantially by selecting and installing the respective cables accordingly. Based on these results, methods of optimising cable layout are proposed such as deviding the system cables into categories and the minimum distances to be kept between the various categories during installation of cables in the system. Thus, a decisive method of guaranteeing the EMC of a system is illustrated by means of various tables, diagrams etc. rendering a survey on the activities carried out and the results obtained; these can be taken as useful source information for specific recommendations and conclusions.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Integral Equations for Transient Scattering
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A numerical technique for transient scattering using time domain integral equations is described. The algorithm uses both MFIE and EFIE equations coupled with a third equation for the charge density on the surface. An implicit algorithm is built which allows to use unequal surface patches to model a structure. The way to solve junction problems between surfaces and wire antennas is indicated. Results obtained, applicable to the hardening of systems are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis and Measurements of Electromagnetic Scattering by Pyramidal Absorbers
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some basic tests and analysis have been performed on absorber material in order to help optimize their use in shielded rooms. By modifying the diffraction coefficients in the Uniform Geometrical Theory an approximation for the scattering from pyramidal absorber (polyurethan) is obtained. This modification is implemented in the cone diffraction solution. In the simulation, measured absorber conductivity and permittivity values are used. Measured scattered fields from an absorber array are compared to calculated results.

articleTitle: A Simple Way of Evaluating the Shielding Effectiveness of Small Enclosures
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Many articles and papers have been published on the virtues of the shielding effectiveness of composite materials. However, the laboratory method of testing has not produced results that are easily correlatable to a practical enclosure for a commercial product. This has caused many manufacturers to shy away from using composite plastics, because the claims of shielding effectiveness in tightly controlled laboratory tests have not been realized in the production of commercial products.

articleTitle: Influence of Electromagnetic Fields on Electro-Explosive Devices (EED)
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the vicinity of powerful radio transmitters RF energy can penetrate into firing circuits used for blasting purposes and can cause permature detonation if the energy is strong enough. The paper describes investigations, done by members of the German VDE working group 764.0.2, for establishing a first draft of the new safety standard "DIN VDE 0848 - Hazards by electromagnetic fields: Influences of electromagnetic fields on bridgefuses for blasting techniques". The purpose of this standard is to give safety distances from radio-frequency transmitters which take into account frequency, modulation and power of the transmitter in regard along with the geometry and the electrical data of the blasting circuit.

articleTitle: Coupling of a Lightning Discharge to Buried Cables
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between predicted and measured currents and voltages induced on buried telecommunication cables by a lightning discharge. The electromagnetic field radiated by the return stroke is calculated, taking the finite ground conductivity into account. Then, knowing the horizontal electric field in the ground, the induced current is determined through the transmission line theory. Experimental results have been obtained at the triggered lightning station situated near St Privat d'Allier, France and also at various points of the telecommunication network where disturbances are stored continuously.

articleTitle: Surface Burst EMP Environments and Coupling
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we review the physical mechanisms leading to late time electromagnetic fields in the source region of a surface nuclear explosion, and discuss simple analytic models of the source region environment. The source of the late time fields is the current produced by the forward motion of the Compton electrons ejected from air atoms by gamma rays. At the times of interest, the gamma rays are created by capture of neutrons in the ground and air. The motion of the Compton electrons can be substantially modified by the turning of the electrons in the EMP magnetic fields. This paper discusses models which are useful for estimating late time fields within four kilometers of a megaton sized burst. We will also discuss the calculation of the current on a long overhead cable at late times, discussing an analytic solution for spatial diffusion in inhomogeneous material which is applicable.

articleTitle: Identification of the Nature of Wideband Spurious Radiations: Experimental Aspects
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The main cause of spurious radiation are parasitic signal conversions in electronic circuitry, resulting in spurious signals either with several discrete frequencies (e. g., when a single frequency signal is passed through a nonlinear inertialess device) or whith a continuous spectrum. In this latter case, spurious radiation may be caused by random fluctuations or to be the result of inherent complex dynamics of the processes taking place in electronic circuitry - dynamic chaos [1].

articleTitle: Getting Better Results from an Open Area Test Site
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Despite a superficial simplicity, an Open Area Test Site has many mechanisms that can cause significant measurement errors. This is exemplified by the disappointing results that too often emerge from Industry efforts to achieve correlation among various sites, particularly with vertical polarization. The most significant sources of error can be identified and either greatly reduced or better understood. This paper will treat the subjects of cable related error, verification of antenna calibration, influence of height on antenna factor, use of averaging to remove antenna calibration errors, characterization of site quality with “Site Uncertainty” measurements, and selection of materials for OATS building construction.

articleTitle: Interference Effects in CMOS and TTL Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study of interference effects on the logical states of TTL and CMOS integrated circuits. The effect of injection of disturbing signals on identical circuits but of CMOS and TTL technologies allows to compare the susceptibility of these components. Only upsets are described and not permanent damages due to the source of interference. However the interpretation of the experimental results is difficult since any measurement can be made inside the integrated circuits. In order to get a qualitative and quantitative prediction of the effects of the disturbance sources, we also describe an experimental set up based on simple components such as bipolar discrete transistors and MOS transistors.

articleTitle: The Far Field of a Horizontally Polarized Dipole Simulator with a Short Rise-Time Pulser
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The far fields from an HPD simulator have been measured and a theory for the radial radiation was developed. It has been shown that in the vicinity of the antenna, the peak amplitude declines with 1/r, where r is the distance. However, at longer distances, the peak amplitude in the radial direction declines with 1/r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This faster decline starts at a distance which easily can be determined by consideration of the geometry and the pulse generator rise-time.

articleTitle: What Future for EMI Instrumentation and Test Methods?
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design of a product for electromagnetic compatibility involves three phases: the initial hardware design, pre-compliance evaluation of the product, and final compliance verification. For each of these phases, more efficient approaches will be developed to reduce product development time and cost. Electromagnetic compatibility between products will increasingly be addressed at the design stage. Combined with extensive precompliance evaluation, improved test methods, and faster instrumentation, this will lead to fewer redesign cycles and lower-cost solutions. The open-site tests of today for radiated emissions from commercial products will largely be replaced by automated tests in shielded, absorber-lined chambers.

articleTitle: Closed-Form Approximative Formula for the near Field of Bent Wire Structures
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Nearfield plots of pulse driven straight line dipoles /1, 2/ show that reasons for radiation from thin wire structures (Fig. 1) can be found in the antenna ends and in the feeding point. From a more generalized point of view, including bends along the wire structures, one would expect radiation not only from the discontinuities mentioned above but also from the additional discontinuities "bends".

articleTitle: International Aspects of Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is my privilege to present an introductory overview for this session on managing the radio spectrum. The session has a distinctly international character, from Mr. Berrada's report on the International Frequency Registion Board, to Professor Radicelle's view of spectrum management in developing countries and Dr. Stumper's global review of spectrumusing services beyond the year 2000.

articleTitle: High Power Electromagnetics: A Generalization of EMP Technology
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Over the last 27 years, EMP technology has been developed by a group of scientists and engineers to the point that many facets of EMP environment specification, simulation, and hardening have become engineering disciplines. The same methodology is now being applied to other elements of high power electromagnetics (HPE): lightning and high power microwaves.

articleTitle: Spectrum Managment in Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper is an attempt to look at the problem of spectrum management in developing countries from a realistic viewpoint based on the understanding of the actual conditions of telecommunications in the context of the social and economic development of those countries. After an appraisal of present time conditions of spectrum management and the possible alternatives for the determination of its economic value, it is suggested that a substantial improvement could be obtained if the concept of "opportunity cost" is adopted. The intervening components of this cost are described. Through the discussion it is shown that, in order to improve spectrum management through this kind of evaluation, the administrations should increase their technical ability by means of well trained personnel.

articleTitle: Transient Response and Transfer Characteristics of EMC/EMP Protection Circuits Containing Nonlinear Filter Pin Connectors
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Protection circuits (with non-linear components) against LEMP- and NEMP-induced interfering currents are of special interest. In case of NEMP interfering signals steepnesses with values up to lo kV/ns may occur. Concerning the overvoltage protection of electronic aircraft systems the protection circuits have to show low weight and small dimensions. These characteristics are of special significance because in case of multiconductor transmission lines a lot of protection circuits have to be installed. Special protection and filter circuits with regard to non-linear filter pin connectors (FPC), have been developed and tested by LEMP and NEMP interfering signals.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Interference Problems for 3-D Wire Structures and Screens
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An interconnection system for electronic components can be modelled as a configuration of conducting wires and screens. The Norton representation of such a configuration provides a complete description for electronic design purposes. A numerical method for solving the Electric Field Integral Equation is implemented to compute these Norton parameters where arbitrary topologies of wires and screens soldered together are allowed for. A design/analysis tool is introduced, which can be helpful in pointing out, by computation, those parts of the configuration responsible for a particular interference problem.

articleTitle: Interference Suppressions using Adaptive Spread-Spectrum Techniques
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper explains why adaptive techniques are essential for effective interference suppressions, discusses the advantages and limitations of adaptive array and spread spectrum techniques to justify the merits of integrating such systems, and to show how to integrate these systems. Adaptive interference suppression techniques are necessary to cope with complicated unpredictable interference conditions. Both adaptive arrays and spread spectrum techniques are capable of rejecting interference without knowing the sources and directions of the interference, but may still be vulnerable to certain types of interference under unfavorable conditions. The merit of integrating such systems has been demonstrated in that they are compatible and complimentary to each other for suppressing interference.

articleTitle: A Study of the Effect of Wave Impedance on Antenna Factors during Screen Room Measurements
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This report investigates the antenna related uncertainty introduced when measuring fields with field impedances other than 377 Ohms. Screen room measurements are typically made at 1 m. This places them in the near-field, for much of the spectrum of interest. Nearfield readings are susceptible to any effects arising from variation in the field impedance. This report compares the response of some common types of antennas to various field impedances. There is a common assumption that a given antenna design primarily responds to only the E-field or H-field. In fact an antenna's antenna factor documents its transfer function to the field used to calibrate the antenna. Hence, the antenna factor is the antennas response to a given field impedance. This study expands on a previous effort, mounted to correlate the screen room measurements made at two different laboratories. The result of that study was the identification of five different antenna related factors which introduce potential errors into screen rooms measurements. This present study focuses on the largest potential error factor found, the effect of field impedance on antenna factor.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in European EMC Standards and Regulations
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A review is given of developments during the last few years with respect to European EMC standards issued by the European Standardization Organization CENELEC and EEC legislation relating to these standards. After an explanation of the functioning of CENELEC, a survey is given of the EMC standards adopted and the resulting consequences for the national standards of the CENELEC member states. The recent EEC Directive on EMC is discussed, as well as its consequences for the EEC member states, EFTA countries and manufacturers of equipment which is subject to this Directive.

articleTitle: Relationship of Lightning Electromagnetic Fields and Currents—An Analytical Approach
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic fields emitted by lightning are an important source of information about the lightning flash, if tools are available to properly interpret the data. In this paper, two analytical tools are exploited to relate electromagnetic spectra and waveforms with the current and other observables so that lightning standards can be more easily established. The first tool is an electromagnetic field solution for a given current distribution. That solution is used to demonstrate a few features of lighting electromagnetic spectra. The second model is a nonlinear, nonuniform transmission line model which predicts the lightning currents as they evolve from a set of initial conditions. In this paper, that model is combined with a simple field model to predict the high frequency electromagnetic fields emitted by lightning at the very beginning of the return stroke.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Screening: An Improved Approximation Based on the Franceschetti Model
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The late-time internal magnetic fields of screened enclosures subjected to pulsed electro-magnetic fields is of continuing interest, not least because of the lack of agreement between theory and experiment. An approach due to Franceshetti leads to simple expressions for the internal field of a spherical screen which are related to the circuit model of screening. The approximation is based on the idea of reducing the three region screening problem to a two region problem with discontinuous fields at the boundary, this latter problem being solved exactly. Further approximations are then introduced based on parameter magnitudes and the functional behaviour of the solution. An inconsistency in the approximation procedure involves the appearance of the screen thickness. Its introduction is equivalent to assuming a uniform distribution of the current, whereas the skin effect will cause the bulk of the current to flow near the outside surface. This paper considers the result of modifying the approximation to take some account of this non-uniform current distribution.

articleTitle: Making Accurate and Repeatable Measurements of the ESD Current Waveform at 1 GHZ AND ABOVE
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Expanding waveform measurements of ESD events from both human and simulator sources to the regime of 1GHz and above has unearthed a variety of new types of error and noise which were masked by the bandwidth limitations of previous techniques. Principal new error sources include radiation of electromagnetic fields associated with the discharge directly into the oscilloscope electronics and CRT, ringing and overshoot from improperly designed current viewing resistors (termed targets) and amplitude errors of the initial spike from loss in the cable used to connect the target to the oscilloscope. These error sources are described along with the accurate measurement techniques that have been developed to circumvent them. Examples are given of the waveform aberrations, and the often significant errors that can result from non optimized equipment and procedures.

articleTitle: Transfer of Norms through Black Boxes
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper addresses the contribution of exciting waveforms and filter characteristics to the response of some ideal black box. Taking the excitation, filter, and response in norm sense, various characteristics of the excitation are examined for their effect on response. We find that the frequency spectral characteristics of the excitation waveform are very important for this purpose. This is true whether one is considering some ideal excitation specification, or one is considering a set of damped sinusoidal excitations.

articleTitle: Some Expected EMI Effects Due to Switching of Electromechanical Relays
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The most common type of relay utilized for switching of electrical signals, is the electromechanical solenoid (EMS) type relay. The solenoid has, typically, a large inductance creating high EMI transients when the coil circuit current is interrupted. The collapsing magnetic fields generate high voltages (due to the Lentz Effect), which appear as CE and RE type interference to other susceptible equipment [l],[3]. The interference emitted by such a relay was detected and measured. This paper discusses the expected effects of a switching EMS relay on neighbouring airborne equipment, in general, and communication equipment, in particular.

articleTitle: Performance Tests of Radiation Hazard Monitors at Frequencies below 30 MHz
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: About 100 radiation hazard monitors of different types from several manufacturers have been tested in TEM cells. The tests have shown that users of commercially available monitors may have to deal with fairly high measuring uncertainties, when the instruments are being used in fields of unknown structure, e.g. near fields.

articleTitle: A New Approach to General EMC Standards
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A strong need for EMC standards initiated the preparation of a set of standards, which are based on a new approach using environmental classes as it has been proposed by IEC for other environmental problems such as climatic or mechanical conditions. The paper discusses this approach and examples of environmental classes are given. The aim of the standards is to be universally applicable, and the test methods are based upon proposals in international papers as well as practical experience from many years of EMC testing.

articleTitle: Transient Voltages and Currents in Straight-Wire Structures over a Lossy Half-Space
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Numerical studies of the electrodynamic behaviour of thin-wire antennas in free space near a lossy half space have been treated extensively during the past decades[1,2,3,4]. Usually the investigations consider only simple arrangements such as vertical or horizontal single wire antennas and are carried out in the frequency domain. The results which are presented in this paper partly refer to much more sophisticated structures and include time domain data as well.

articleTitle: Matching Surge Suppressors for Current Sharing
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Parallel connection of suppressor devices results in effective current sharing only when the components are properly matched. Voltage matching can be illusory if measured only at low test currents. Internal resistance matching is equally important. Dynamic impedance matching implies that both voltage and resistance are matched, but two high current tests would be needed. A single clamping voltage test might suffice for MOV devices if some simple rules are followed.

articleTitle: EMI from AC Traction Lines: Field Measurements on Telecommunication Cables
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A considerable problem in railway electrifications adopting a.c. systems is the electromagnetic influence the overhead lines produce on telecommunication cables and other long metallic structures laid along the tracks.

articleTitle: Global Distribution of Power Line Harmonics Radiation and Natural VLF Emission Observed by the Ohzora Satellite
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The global distribution of the electric field intensities of the power line harmonics radiation (PLHR) in the topside ionosphere has been measured by the on board instrument of the satellite "OHZORA". This observation started June 1st, 1984 and continues until today. The observation results show several interesting distribution characteristics of PLR over the world. (1) The largest emissions of PLHR were observed around the northern American continent such as; northern British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, Illinois, Michigan, Quebec and north-eastern U.S. (2) The second largest values were observed around northern Europe, such as; U.K., Germany, east part of the U.S.S.R., Moscow area and along the northern coast of the U.S.S.R.. These noisy areas are spread along the northern auroral oval and this explains the source mechanism of PLHR. (3)The authors found new strong natural VLF noise emission at geomagnetical southern Atlantic anomaly region. The authors present the observation results in this paper.

articleTitle: A New Method to Evaluate the Propagation of Electromagnetic Waves on Inhomogeneous Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The increasing use of modern electronic components along with classic electric devices in vehicles requires detailed knowledge about electromagnetic interference on automotive cables. The work presented here extends the transmission line theory to handle nonuniformly shaped transmission lines. This is a more realistic approach to automotive cables. The method is based upon the modified solution of the transmission line equations for inhomogeneous lines with low losses deduced by K. W. Wagner [1]. The algorithm was applied to a homogeneous line m order to compare these results to an exact solution, found by an analytic calculation. The input impedance of a mismatched, periodically inhomogeneous transmission line was calculated, and the results were compared to measured data.

articleTitle: A New ESO Test Method and its Impact
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The first ESD standard introduced to the EMC community was the IEC 801-2. This IEC standard was developed in the early 80's and published in 1984. During recent experience with the ESD test in accordance with IEC 801-2 it was noticed that the test method has a lot of deficiencies. The main weakness is the extremly poor repeatability of the test results. A new test method solving the problem of repeatability is suggested in TC65 (SEC) 129 and ECMA TR40. This new test method and some experience with real events in the laboratory are described in this report.

articleTitle: Accelerated and Easier EMI Tests
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Measurement speed in EMI tests is influenced by the complexity of the testing philosophy which is greatly determined by the EMI measurement standards. The paper tries to show what measures can be taken to save time in automated EMI tests while being in line with the existing standards. Furtheron trends in EMI measurement standards and their impact on automated testing are analyzed as well as the impact of some recent solutions to improve radiated EMI measurements.

articleTitle: Electrical Simulation of Multi Layer PCB with Non-Parallel Tracks and Printed Components
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A Boundary Element Method (BEM) solution for the 3D electromagnetic fields In a variety of printed circuit board structures is presented. These structures include multi-layer boards, with or without a parallel conducting plane, which need not be coincident with a surface of the PCB. Any number of metallisation layers with different conductivities are allowed, and these may contain a large number of non-parallel tracks, rectangular or circular solder pads, and printed components such as spiral inductors or interdigital capacitors. Good agreement between the model and measurement is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Radio-Interference Voltage Produced by Television Receivers: A Statistical Investigation
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An experimental investigation on a sample of modern television receivers has been carried out to study the influence of the test picture, the ground connection and the type of detector on the measurement of interference voltages injected into the mains. Emission measurements were performed with a spectrum analyzer (with quasi-peak adapter and preselector, when necessary) controlled by a personal computer and a software developed to automatize the measurements and the data processing. The investigation allowed also to statistically analyse narrow-band and broad-band interference produced by modern television receivers, such as digital clocks, switching power supplies, colour sub-carriers.

articleTitle: Television Interference and Audible Noise Caused by HV Lines. Laboratory and Field Test Results
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of interference measurements on 400 and 750 kV transmission lines at frequencies above 30 MHz are presented. Instruments meeting technical characteristics of the CISPR requirements were used. Frequency spectra of interference and interference attenuation along the line and in the lateral direction were gained. The rate of interference intensity growth for artificial gaps of different sizes was determined. The results of laboratory measurements of audible noise for bundle conductors with different diameters and for different conductor surface gradients are given. Frequency spectra of audible noise from a 750 kV transmission line using various instruments and microphones were obtained.

articleTitle: Instrumentation Variability in EMI Tests on Open Area Test Sites
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses errors caused in open area EMI tests by the variability of the test instrumentation. The log-normal distribution is used as a statistical model by which to estimate errors. The errors arrising from variability in antennas, transmission lines and input circuits of instruments, and other instrument variability, are considered.

articleTitle: Establishing Immunity Limits when the Determining Factors are Correlated
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Questions of the receptors immunity parameters establishment for the most common case are considered when the environment vector components, for example, radiated and conducted interferences or corresponding receptor immunity parameters are correlated. It's shown that with non-correlated influencing factors establishment of the limits system for receptor immunity parameters leads to more rigit requirements comparing with the case when influencing factors are correlated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Cylindrical Shield Efficiency using a Variational Approach
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An approach using finite element method in the time domain, is presented in the case of the penetration of transient fields through thin cylindrical shields of arbitrary cross-section. Then, numerical results are compared with an available analytical solution The proposed method is found to be very accurate and to converge very rapidly. Examples of inhomogeneous shields are also presented to demonstrate the flexibility of the method which, with some modifications, can be easily extended to more complex geometries.

articleTitle: A New Universal Algorithm for Computation of Interference by Earth Return Currents
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a universal, exact physical-mathematical model able to simulate AC and OC interference of any given complexity from external flow field on nearby underground conductors. The model in the form of an active two-port with a current source representing the external influence enables one to calculate any interference due to inductive and conductive couplings. Efficient techniques of calculation of the scalar potential of the flow field in the earth near the equipotential as well as non-equipotential earthing arrangements are presented in the paper. The method is illustrated with examples of calculations.

articleTitle: New Approach to the International Management of the Spectrum and the Geostationary-Satellite Orbit
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The need for regulating radiocommunications was recognized early in this century. The first international Regulations had left aside economical aspects of the use of radio frequencies which were closely related to competitive techniques ; the Regulations were limited to mainly a short and simple Table of Frequency Allocations and few provisions relating to the operation of mobile services. The conformity with this Table was only recommended and the frequency uses were communicated to a central Bureau in Berne for recording in a list (Bern List) without any legal status being derived from this recording. The Table was progressively up-dated in conferences held before the war but the overall situation did not change. The rapid technological advances achieved during the period of the war rendered necessary more stringent regulations to avoid any chaotic situation which may result from an increased number of users and which will be detrimental to all uses mainly to those involving the safety of human life. The 1947 Atlantic City Conference set up the foundation of the current international management system of the frequency spectrum. It was preceded by several years of preparation which culminated at the Moscow meeting in 1946. The system established by the Atlantic City Conference is based on : - a set of provisions specifying the way in which the spectrum may be used and the procedures to be applied by administrations; - the creation of a new permanent organ, the International Frequency Registration Board (IFRB) to decide on the conformity with the above rules and to record formally each use in the Master International Frequency Register (MIFR) thus defining its legal status. A detailed review of these two constituents and their evolution during these last decades may be useful in considering the future evolution of the system.

articleTitle: Designing for Electrostatic Discharge Immunity
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper analyzes how Electronic Systems can be designed to be immune to Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) in a cost effective manner. These four major design areas are examined; Grounding, Circuit Board Design, Cable and Harness Design, and the Mechanical Enclosure (Covers). This paper will show how these immunity control techniques are applied to the systems containing the latest processor designs.

articleTitle: A Refined Mathematical Model Applied to a Multilayer Board
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the past several mathematical models [1-4] have been developed to predict the emissions from printed circuit boards (PCB), The method of moment in an earlier work [1] was used to calculate the electric fields emanated from a PCB in the 30-200 MHz frequency band; however, the effects of trace discontinuities, such as sharp bends, open-ends, have been ignored. A refined modeling technique included the discontinuity effects is presented in this paper. A radiated structure which was modeled by using several straight round wires was composed of a portion of clock trace, board ground plane and reflected earth ground. The discontinuities were modeled by the equivalent ideal capacitors and inductors elements connected at the discontinuities. A higher correlation than previously reported [1], between measured and calculated data, is obtained.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Absorber Measurement in a Large Waveguide
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A large three-sectional waveguide of 24.5 meters length (not including the absorber carriage) has been built in Westerlo. It allows absorber reflectivity measurements to be done in the 85-325 MHz frequency range. The carriage accommodates six standard-size (i.e. with a base of 61 cm x 61 cm) absorbers and can be slided up to 4.8 m into the waveguide. The reflectivity measured equals the true free-space metal-backed reflectivity. The equivalent free-space incident plane wave is perpendicularly polarised (i.e. TE) and has a frequency dependent angle of incidence varying between 7° and 29°. The paper describes the design and construction of this waveguide from an electromagnetic viewpoint. Both a single-frequency measurement technique using standard QC (Quality Control) equipment and a swept-frequency technique using an advanced automatic network analyser, are outlined. Both techniques yield virtually identical results. By way of illustration, some representative swept-frequency measurement results are given.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Interference Problems in Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Increased demand for frequency spectrum and the constraints of geostationary satellite orbit require the development of more efficient sharing techniques. Interference assessment for radio communications systems have usually been based on the deterministic nature using worst-case conditions. This paper introduces statistical approaches to interference problems in satellite communication systems to achieve a better understanding of the implications of sharing conditions. Sidelobe characteristics of a small earth station antenna, the distribution of C/I value in a service area, and relations between single and aggregated interference criteria are discussed.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of a Modification to the Transmission Line Model for Lemp Calculations
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a proposed modification to the Transmission Line model for LEMP calculations is analyzed and tested by using existing experimental results. The new model, in which the current pulse intensity is allowed to decrease with height above ground, yields satisfactory approximations to the electric and magnetic fields measured at far and close stations. The derived lightning return stroke velocities as well as the current shapes at ground level are reasonably consistent with experimental data. The new model is then adopted to calculate the electromagnetic field originated by a typical mean current shape measured at ground. The calculated fields exhibit features which are typical of experimental ones. All the tests are performed for both the new model and the original one, showing that the proposed modification highly improves the agreement with experimental data.

articleTitle: A Methodology to Assess Exo-Nemp Impact on a Real System - Case Studies
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A systematical, theoretical as well as experimental approach to assess EMP-impact on real systems is outlined. The systems considered are an electromechanical locomotive, a private telephone branch exchange system, and a small digital encryption unit. In spite of the different sizes of the systems the same simulation techniques - field excitation and current injection - are used, resulting in different system responses (upset - damage). Some of these results are presented and analyzed in light of the weighting between conducted and radiated interference phenomena to help establish realistic and economical test methods.

articleTitle: Emission and Susceptibility Testing in a Tapered Tem Cell
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of a tapered TEM cell - anechoic chamber hybrid for radiated emission and susceptibility testing is discussed. The TEM mode is used to simulate a plane wave for susceptibility testing (both CW and pulsed), as with a standard TEM cell. Within the recommended test volume, field uniformity varies with both position (+/-1 dB) and frequency (+/- 3 dB for dc to 1 GHz). Thus, an overall field uniformity of +/- 4 dB within the recommended test volume is presently achievable. The test volume size may be scaled upwards at the loss of only field strength. For the emission case, test object radiation is modeled with an equivalent multi-pole expansion. The dominant terms of the multi-pole expansion may be determined through a sequence of cell measurements. These dominant terms may then be used to predict test object radiation both in free space and over a ground screen. In this manner time consuming emission measurements, such as those required by FCC Rules Part 15 Subpart J or VDE 0871, may be simulated numerically. Both experimental and theoretical data are presented. The advantages and limitations of this cell design with respect to other popular methods are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Class a Narrowband Radio Noise Simulation
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two algorithms of narrowband random processes stimulation described by D. Middleton canonical models of class A natural and man-made interferences are offered. One of the algorithms is based on identity with Ya. Likhter atmospheric interferences model extended to the case of overlapping pulses of D. Middleton class A interference model. Another algorithm represents class A interference component as a stationary narrowband Gaussian process modulated by birth and death process. It is shown that the use of Gaussian and Poisson random processes is sufficient for the algorithms realization. Comparison of algorithms is made and simulation error due to truncation of class A interference one dimensional distribution is estimated.

articleTitle: Threshold Vector Field Estimators in Non-Gaussian EMC Environments
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The present paper extends the author's earlier work [1H4] on weak signal estimation in electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) environments to include simultaneous space-time signal processing of vector (electromagnetic) fields. Specifically, the emphasis here is on signal intensity and waveform estimation in telecommunications, where typically desired signals are narrowband, are received in the far-field, and have well-defined wavefronts, subject to directional transmission and reception.
