The principal interference is other similar ”intelligent" transmissions and can include both natural and man-made "unintelligent" interference, e.g., atmospheric noise, automobile ignition effects, etc. A principal aim of the present study is to establish limits on the reconstruction (“extraction") of desired signal waveforms in crowded spectral regions, where the Interference is usually highly "structured" and nongaussian, and to determine the extent to which taking account of the vector nature of both signal and interference can modify and potentially improve the process of signal recovery. A high level of generality is postulated, including general signals and geometries. The resulting processing algorithms are new, reducing to familiar (and earlier) forms when the interference is gaussian. Optimum maximum likelihood estimators are constructed in the threshold régimes, based on the associated optimum threshold detection algorithms. Again, three principal modes of reception are considered: (i) coherent; (ii) incoherent; and (ill) composite, which require different algorithmic structures. An important result is the potentially large (O(10-30 dB) or more) degradation in estimation accuracy encountered when conventional estimators based on gaussian noise are employed, paralleling a similar effect in similar detection situations [2], These vector estimation algorithms are expectedly more complex than the scalar field cases, but remain explicitly manageable. Examples are included, as well as a comparison of systems in typical, nongaussian interference environments.

articleTitle: Splitting of Degenerate Eigenvalues in Coupled Two- and Three-Conductor Lines
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents several simple modeling concepts useful for analysing the response of complex (sub) systems with strongly coupled cables. Cables do no longer behave like individuals when they run close to other cables. Based on transmission line theory it is pointed out that a combination of coupling and (natural) properties of metallic conductors, e.g. internal inductance and resistance, removes degeneracy of eigenstates and causes frequency splitting, a fact which is also important for understanding a certain class of beat. The splitting predicted by theory is confirmed by experimental data. Numerical field calculations point in the same direction. In a prospect other mechanisms with similiar effects are discussed.

articleTitle: EMC/EMP Protection in Naval Vessels
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electronic equipment in naval vessels is vulnerable to conducted and radiated interference from the vessels own installations and to electromagnetic radiations from external sources. This paper discusses the advantages taken of the screening inherent in ships of metallic construction and the additional precautions necessary with the new generations of G.R.P vessels.

articleTitle: The Natural Electromagnetic Field in Central Asia
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In present report the results of the experimental study of natural electromagnetic field (NEMF) in the range from ones to hundreds Hz made in Central Asia over the years 1973-1987, are summerised. Basic regularities of the NEMF space-time and spectral distributions for the region distant from the world thunderstorm activity centers have been ascertained. The structure of the NEMF space components at the Earth-air interface has been investigated. The characteristics of the global resonances of the Earth-ionosphere cavity have been considered. The NEMF data obtained during disturbed geophysical conditions (solar eclipce, local earthquake) have been analyzed. A NEMF application for the determination of Earth conductivity have been considered.

articleTitle: Pulse Coupling to Slit Cylinders
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The coupling of a fast transient pulsed field to a wire enclosed by a long circular cylinder with a slit parallel to the wire is examined. Mathematical prediction and experimental measurements are compared.

articleTitle: Some Characteristic Signatures of Power Disturbances on AC Mains
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Early investigators of mains disturbances employed oscilloscopes and oscillographic recorders [1] [5], but with the introduction of portable digital mains disturbance analyzers in the early 1970’s, most investigators' attention shifted to statistical summaries of the amplitude of various mains disturbances. Oscillographic recording was reserved primarily for harmonics investigations, such as those described in references [7] and [8].

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility between Underground Trains using Power Inverters and Signalling Audio-Frequency Systems
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The interference problems caused by inverters installed on trains of underground railways are considered. The interference spectra have been measured and the results compared with the calculated values. The main inverter, which generates a three-phase system to supply the motors, is represented by two different models in order to simulate the traction and breaking working mode. The interference caused by the auxiliary inverter has also been considered and its contribution evaluated separately. The spectra of the current absorbed by the train were measured using a spectrum analyzer and a test probe, designed for this purpose. Moreover, the interference voltages induced in the loops of the audio-frequency signalling system (AFO) and installed in between the rails were measured and their levels compared to the usual wanted signal levels.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Properties of Steel-Fiber Reinforced Concrete in the RF and Microwave Range
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Dry concrete without metallic reinforcements is rather transparent to electromagnetic waves. For the construction of buildings, which should be shielded against high-frequency electromagnetic radiation, it is proposed to apply steel-fiber reinforced concrete instead of concrete with conventional steel-grid reinforcement. The idea involved is that the statistically distributed steel-fibers, which may be considered as nails or short pieces of thin wire, act as scatterers for the incident electromagnetic waves, thus increasing the transmission losses considerably. Due to multiple scattering and the rather high losses in steel or iron the reflected power is also much smaller than in the case of simple metallic wall shieldings. With attenuation figures of more than 200 dB/m a number of interesting applications seem to be possible.

articleTitle: RF Disturbances on Telephone-Subscriber Lines Induced by am Broadcasting Transmitters
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Large numbers of measurements have been carried out at telephone-subscriber and telephone-exchange sites in Germany, to characterize the common-mode disturbance on the a-b wires, induced by AM broadcasting transmitters in the medium and short wave range. By introducing the effective electrical length of the a-b wires the induced disturbance source can be characterized independently of the transmitter power and the distance to that transmitter. Current-injection yielded information about the impedance of the source. In addition the data provide information about common-mode currents on the a-b wires, building attenuation, unsymmetric voltages induced in the mains network, and simple prediction of field strengths.

articleTitle: Practical Acceptance Tests of Emp Shields
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Main factor affecting to the quality of electromagnetically shielded room-size or building-size enclosures is the care of the construction work. Acceptance tests ordered from an independent research company or performed self, e.g. in case of a telecommunication administration, should always be included in the construction agreements. The test method should be such that all significant defects can be revealed. It should be performed in the earliest possible phase to allow immediate repair. It should not be too time-consuming to mix the usually tight time shedules during construction. EMP shielded data or telecom centres may nowadays form the main part of electromagnetically shielded enclosures. This report describes a test method used in acceptance of several EMP-shielded shelters in Finland. The shielding technique is referred briefly and the test results are discussed.

articleTitle: A New Lightning Current Function for Transients Calculation
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic fields generated by lightning currents may cause damages or interferences in the operation of a majority of electronic and electric systems. It concerns e specially the circuits with sensitive electronic devices in automatic machines and computers. For this reason in this paper a theoretical determination of currents and voltages induced by lightning electromagnetic pulse in simple arrangements of unshielded cables is presented. These calculations are carried out with a help of a new mathematical function which exactly descrebes the shape of the lightning current.

articleTitle: Minimum Attenuation and Input Impedance Domain of a Linear Filter
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is a well established fact that the behaviour and performance of linear filters strongly depend on the impedance connected at its input and output. This observation is of utmost importance when dealing with power line filters. Classically, the characterization of a linear filter is done with the use of a quantity known as insertion loss. We first introduce this quantity together with three other important concepts, namely the total attenuation, the absorption attenuation and the mismatch attenuation. We then define what we call the worst case at the output and the worst case at the input of the filter. We show how to compute insertion loss and attenuations in a worst case. The minimum attenuation of the filter is the absorption attenuation in the worst case (at the output) and is also the total attenuation in the worst case at the output and at the input. The input impedance domain of a filter is defined and shown to be a convenient tool to understand the filter’s behaviour and to compute the mismatch attenuation in a worst case. We show that in many cases, the most relevant quantity for the study of a power line filter is the total attenuation, which can be most easily assessed with the combined use of minimum attenuation and input impedance domain. We compare these new developments In power line filter theory to former studies, which involved the worst case insertion loss or minimum voltage attenuation.

articleTitle: Measurement of Field Distribution in an Absorber-Loaded Tem Cell
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper reports the results of an experimental test program undertaken to develop a modified transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell with expanded bandwidth for use in accurately characterizing electromagnetic interference (EMI) fields within a shielded environment. A TEM cell with the RF absorbing materials on the inside walls is tested to see how suppression of resonances affects the field distribution within the cell.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Ambient Survey in Industries for the Design and Installation of Radio Control and Other Sensitive Electronic Equipment
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper emphasizes the need for electromagnetic ambient measurements in various industries so that the electromagnetic environment where radio control and sensitive electronic equipment have to perform is known. It goes on to describe the various methods of electromagnetic ambient measurements at various industries like thermal power plant, steel plant etc., and presents the actual ambient level data. The paper further discusses the guidelines in accounting the measured ambient levels in the design of radio control for various industrial applications like crane control, robots etc. and in the installation of sensitive electronic equipment. The paper concludes with recommendations on design parameters for radio control applications and tentative recommendations on radiated susceptibility test levels for sensitive electronic equipment to be used in these industries.

articleTitle: How High is the Level of Electromagnetic Fields Radiated by an ESD?
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Quantitative estimation of the electromagnetic fields radiated by electrostatic discharges (ESD) is of importance to the users and computer industry. Analytical and experimental results, based on a new theoretical model and specific measurement system, are presented to achieve this objective. The ESD spark is modeled as an electrically short, time dependent, linear dipole situated above an infinite ground plane. The specific measurement system consists of a newly designed broadband, time-domain TEM horn antenna, a wideband digitizing oscilloscope, and a desktop computer.

articleTitle: EMC Design and Testing of Control Equipment in an 800 kV SF6-gas Insulated Substation
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: When microelectronics, e.g. microprocessors, are installed in secondary equipment of SF6-gas insulated switchgear (GIS), electromagnetic compatibility between these microelectronics and the given electromagnetic environment is essential. This paper describes a coordinated approach to the management of EMC in GIS and is presented in three main sections: - EMC-Analysis The EMC-Analysis describes the main noise sources in GIS and their disturbance variables. The coupling path of these disturbance variables into secondary equipment, the so called noise sinks, are described. With the knowledge of emission limits of various noise sources and the immunity limits of secondary equipment, the margin of electromagnetic compatibility is defined. If the margin is not sufficient, additional measures are necessary. In this paper results of the EMC analysis taken in an 800 kV Pilot Substation are described. - EMC-Measures EMC measures can be performed at the noise source, the coupling path, or secondary equipment. Solutions have to be based on technical and economical objectives. The few described in this paper are the result of EMC planning for an 800 kV substation were microprocessors are installed near the process. - EMC-Verification The verification of EMC takes place during the development phase on several components in the EMC laboratory. After installation of secondary equipment an on-site EMC test demonstrates the correct installation.

articleTitle: Rerouting Lightning Currents in a Communication Tower
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: P. C. T. van der Laan

abstract: A lightning protection system of a telecommunication tower has been tested. In a simulation experiment we measured the current distribution over all leads attached to the tower, together with the voltage differences at sensitive points. The extrapolation of the results to an actual lightning strike are discussed. Suggestions and recommendations for full protection are given.

articleTitle: EMC of Cordless Telephones and 915 MHz ISM Sources
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Leakages from 896/915 MHz ISM installations have been investigated and the electromagnetic compatibility with cordless telephones has been assessed. Levels up to 60 dBμV/m will not interfere with normal operation and leakages are controllable down this level without the need for whole factory faradization. A 900 MHz frequency must be allowed in Europe for ISM provided the leakage levels are limited to 60 dBμV/m at 30 m from the boundary of the premisses. Guidelines are presented for installing ISM apparatus and reducing EMI.

articleTitle: EMP Inductive Injection System
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The system described in this paper was specifically designed for the indirect injection of powerful exponential pulses into long cables to simulate the transients picked by those cables in the event of high altitude burst EMP. The system consists of two 100kV, fast rise time pulse generators, feeding eight modules of large magnetic core transformers, which clamp on the cable under test and couple the energy to it. The system allows the injection of currents up to 2kA and voltages of up to 300kV, depending on the characteristic impedance of the transmission line created by the cable under test and its surroundings. The waveshape of the injected transients is exponential, with rise times of 20-150nsec and decay times around 2μsec.

articleTitle: Theory and Application of Radiated EMI Field Modeling for Pre-Compliance Testing
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Estimates of the worst-case radiated electric field are generated from measurements of the magnetic near-field of a DUT using mathematical models. Unlike existing vector models used for tuning antenna patterns in phased array systems, these scalar models are designed for radiated EMI pre-qualification of shielded instruments. This paper describes the models and discusses the results of their application to the prequalification of a new instrument.

articleTitle: Time-Dependent Lightning-Originated Underground Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: With reference to the induction effects involving horizontally buried extended systems when the environment is affected by a lightning-originated electromagnetic field, an approximate analytical calculation is proposed. The investigation on the field below ground is carried out making use of the transmission line model applied to an upright channel. Further, a realistic frequency-dependent performance of a moist soil is assumed. The wave propagation into ground is performed according to the Sommerfeld analysis.

articleTitle: Prima - A Program for Interactive EMI Matrix Analysis
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A reduced instruction program is proposed to limit overflowing work during EMC system analysis. The paper depicts requirements, conversion, result of work by executed examples. Principle of program is the comparison of maximum emission minus minimum susceptibility of regarded equipments with physical decouplings. The investigation takes place at seven fix frequencies and one but outmost frequency of the special equipment. The worst case including type of program explains why it shall not substitute other methods of analysis but prepare them pointing out the relative few number of real problems. The program has been tested for validitation at more than 20 systems. Accuracy is in the order of about the input accuracy. The program can analyse 500 equipments at a time. Recommended hardware is a XT/AT or compatible PC with 640 K RAM, DOS 3.x, at least one disk drive and hard disk. Assisting programs are a data pool (POOL) with 3.000 equipment to store facility, and the electromagnetic environment (EME) presenting it at arbitrary coordinate at seven fix and all used special frequencies in the system. PRIMA calculates 1000 combinations per minute or a 500 equipment system in 4:10 h under condition that the PC is an 8 MHz AT3 equipped with math- coprocessor.

articleTitle: Potential-Free Spherical Sensor for Fieldstrength Measurement in NEMP Research and Testing
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This contribution describes special spherical field sensors for the measurement of arbitrary oriented electric or magnetic field vectors. The battery-powered sensors have a bandwidth of 100 MHz, a dynamic range of more than 40 dB, and fibreoptic data links. The accuracy of sensors for the measurement of electromagnetic fields depends on their size and their shape. The principal geometry of the sensors dealed with in this contribution is a conducting hollow sphere. For such a sphere in this case with a diameter of 10 cm the field components inside, in the wall of the sphere, and outside of the sphere can be calculated in the frequency domain. From these calculations theoretical values for the limit of the stationary behaviour of the spherical sensors are deduced. For the accuracy of the measurement with these sensors in inhomogeneous fields theoretical limits are deduced from the static and the stationary approach respectively. The realized measuring system with these sensors, their characteristics and some typical measuring results are given.

articleTitle: Spectrum Demanding Services into the Year 2000 and Beyond
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The new services, that are integrated with existing services in ISDN need a broader spectrum. Moreover the mobile services have a sharp increase in their number of customers, and thus on their demand on the radio spectrum. They too wish to have some of the ISDN services available. Opinions are divided on the possibility of wide introduction of BISDN, without the use of the radio (satellite communication) spectrum. If some of the services, now using the microwave services, could go over to fibre optics, the necessary room for mobile service extension would be available.

articleTitle: Modeling Electronic System Radiated Field Patterns
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radiated field pattern techniques are used to study electronic system emissions. The paper explores the relationship between the electronic system design and configuration ana its EMI potential. An electronic system is considered as consisting of a set of magnetic and electric EMI sources. To model its radiated field, a concept of an active antenna array is introduced. The developed models are utilised to synthesize and analyze real electronic system radiating fields, explain and interpret EMC test results, ana arrive at important practical recommendations.

articleTitle: Selecting Varistor Clamping Voltage: Lower is not Better !
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Surge protective devices, such as varistors, are applied to protect sensitive load equipment against power-line surges. The need to provide low clamping voltage for protection of equipment with low inherent immunity must be balanced against the risk of premature aging of the protective device. Lower clamping voltage causes more frequent interventions of the protective device, accelerating its aging. The paper describes four possible causes of such premature aging, calling for a more careful and thus more reliable application of protective devices.

articleTitle: Standard Waveforms for Surge Testing: Experimental Evaluation and Proposed new Criteria for Tolerances
publicationTitle: 8th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An experimental evaluation was conducted to compare waveforms from high-voltage surge generators to the waveform specifications. Generators from three major manufacturers were evaluated for (1) the combination 1.2/50 μs voltage and 8/20 μs current waveform and (2) the 100 kHz ring wave specified in ANSI C62.41-1980. Changes in the waveform when the surge generator was connected to metal-oxide varistors or a 0.1 μF capacitor were also described. Finally, proposals are made for more complete specifications for the 1.2/50 and 8/20 μs waveforms.
